steps.name: Move Linear
steps.description: Move to a target in a straight line.

params.label: Target
params.help: A saved point, a $points[i] element, a template naming a point, a grid or stack cell — or nothing for the current position (use with offsets).

params.label: Speed
params.help: Overrides the program's speed for this move only.

params.label: Blend into next move
params.help: Round the corner into the next move instead of stopping.

params.label: Blend radius
params.help: Empty = the radius set by Set Blend Radius.

params.label: Offset
params.help: Added to the target (relative move when there is no target).

params.label: Override
params.help: Replaces an axis of the target outright.

params.label: Tool offset
params.help: Applied in the tool frame at execution time.

params.label: Local frame
params.help: Run this move in a local frame instead of the active one.

params.label: Stop condition
params.help: Watched every tick while the move runs, e.g. $io.Nano.Load >= 2000.

params.label: Position variable
params.help: A Points list set to the one pose where the condition fired.

params.label: Fired flag
params.help: Set to 1 if the condition fired during the move, else 0.

notes: The tool centre point travels a straight line in Cartesian space.

`blend=on` (or `blend=<radius>`) rounds the corner into the next blend-enabled move instead of stopping; consecutive blended moves run as one continuous path. Without a radius the value from Set Blend Radius is used.
A Move Linear with a stop condition never blends.

The target is resolved from the first of: a grid cell, a stack slot, a `$list[i]` element or template (`pointNameExpr`), a saved point. With no target the move starts from the current position, so `offset=` makes it relative.
`offset=` is added to the target, `set=` replaces an axis outright, `toolOffset=` is applied in the tool frame; each axis may be an expression.
Program moves are scaled by the operator's speed override and by Set Speed Factor.
Not run in background programs (motion is skipped there).

A stop condition (`until=`) is checked every controller tick while the move runs. `untilMode=stop` ends the move where it is and continues with the next step (no error); `record` lets the move finish and stores the pose where the condition first held in `untilPos=` (a one-element Points list). `untilFlag=` gets 1 if it fired, else 0.

errors.label: Point not found
errors.when: A template or `$list[i]` target names no saved point, or the Points list is empty.

errors.label: Motion fault
errors.when: The motion system reports a fault (fatal).

errors.label: Joint limit
errors.when: The target is outside a joint's soft limits (fatal).

errors.label: Driver disconnected
errors.when: The motor driver is not connected (fatal).

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
MoveL Approach, speed=150
MoveL Pick1, offset=(z=20), blend=5
MoveL Pick1

steps.name: Jump Linear
steps.description: Lift, move linearly over the target, then lower.

params.label: Target
params.help: A saved point, a $points[i] element, a template naming a point, a grid or stack cell — or nothing for the current position (use with offsets).

params.label: Lift height
params.help: Z used for the lift and lower legs.

params.label: Lift height (start)
params.help: Overrides the lift leg only.

params.label: Lift height (end)
params.help: Overrides the lower leg only.

params.label: Speed
params.help: Overrides the program's speed for this move only.

params.label: Blend into next move
params.help: Round the corner into the next move instead of stopping.

params.label: Blend radius
params.help: Empty = the radius set by Set Blend Radius.

params.label: Offset
params.help: Added to the target (relative move when there is no target).

params.label: Override
params.help: Replaces an axis of the target outright.

params.label: Tool offset
params.help: Applied in the tool frame at execution time.

params.label: Local frame
params.help: Run this move in a local frame instead of the active one.

params.label: Stop condition
params.help: Watched every tick while the move runs, e.g. $io.Nano.Load >= 2000.

params.label: Position variable
params.help: A Points list set to the one pose where the condition fired.

params.label: Fired flag
params.help: Set to 1 if the condition fired during the move, else 0.

notes: Three legs: lift straight up to `z=`, travel over the target at that height, lower onto the target. `zStart=` / `zEnd=` set the lift and lower heights separately.
Blending applies to the traverse leg.
With a stop condition the jump takes the stepped (non-blended) path and the watch spans all three legs; in stop mode the remaining legs are skipped.

The target is resolved from the first of: a grid cell, a stack slot, a `$list[i]` element or template (`pointNameExpr`), a saved point. With no target the move starts from the current position, so `offset=` makes it relative.

Program moves are scaled by the operator's speed override and by Set Speed Factor.
Not run in background programs (motion is skipped there).

errors.when: The motor driver is not connected (fatal).

JumpL grid Tray[2, 1], z=40, zEnd=50

steps.name: Move Arc
steps.description: Move along a circular arc through a via point to the end target.

params.label: Target
params.help: A saved point, a $points[i] element, a template naming a point, a grid or stack cell — or nothing for the current position (use with offsets).

params.label: Via point
params.help: A point the arc passes through (saved point, $points[i] element or template).

params.label: Speed
params.help: Overrides the program's speed for this move only.

params.label: Arc tolerance
params.help: Largest allowed gap between the true arc and its straight segments.

params.label: Offset
params.help: Added to the target (relative move when there is no target).

params.label: Override
params.help: Replaces an axis of the target outright.

params.label: Local frame
params.help: Run this move in a local frame instead of the active one.

notes: Follows the circle through the start (where the robot is), the via point and the end, in any plane.
The arc is cut into equal chords that stay within `tolerance=` of the true circle (and span at most 2°), sent as one continuous path; the robot stops exactly on the end.
RX / RY / RZ change linearly from the start's to the end's; the via point's orientation is not used.
`offset=`, `set=` and `local=` apply to both the via and the end. Stop conditions are not supported; tool offset and blending are ignored.
Not run in background programs.

errors.label: Arc points are in a line
errors.when: Start, via and end are on one line, or two of them are the same.

errors.label: Point not found
errors.when: The via or end names no saved point.

errors.label: Motion fault
errors.when: The motion system reports a fault (fatal).

errors.label: Joint limit
errors.when: The target is outside a joint's soft limits (fatal).

errors.label: Driver disconnected
errors.when: The motor driver is not connected (fatal).

example.srs:
MoveL Pick1
MoveC Place1, via=Via1, speed=80, tolerance=0.1

steps.name: Thread Move
steps.description: Move the tool in Z while rotating RZ to follow a thread.
steps.syntax: ThreadMove distance=…, pitch=…[, peck=on, peckDepth=…, peckRetract=…][, exitHeight=…][, reverseOut=on]

params.label: Peck retract
params.help: Empty = retract fully to the start each peck.

params.label: Speed
params.help: Overrides the program's speed for this move only.

notes: Moves the tool `distance=` along Z while turning RZ by one revolution per `pitch=` mm — screwing in or tapping.
`peck=on` advances in `peckDepth=` steps, retracting by `peckRetract=` between pecks (empty = back to the start each peck). `exitHeight=` and `reverseOut=on` control how the tool leaves.
Not run in background programs.

errors.label: Motion fault
errors.when: The motion system reports a fault (fatal).

errors.label: Joint limit
errors.when: The target is outside a joint's soft limits (fatal).

errors.label: Driver disconnected
errors.when: The motor driver is not connected (fatal).

example.srs:
MoveL Pick1, offset=(z=5)
ThreadMove distance=-12, pitch=1.25, reverseOut=on

steps.name: Run Homing
steps.description: Run the full homing sequence and wait for it to finish.
notes: Runs the full homing sequence and waits until it finishes.
Not run in background programs.

errors.label: Motion fault
errors.when: The motion system reports a fault (fatal).

errors.label: Joint limit
errors.when: The target is outside a joint's soft limits (fatal).

errors.label: Driver disconnected
errors.when: The motor driver is not connected (fatal).

example.srs:
if not $robot.homed
  RunHoming
end

steps.name: Set Joint Position
steps.description: Declare one joint's value with no motion (manual homing).
notes: Declares the current value of one joint without moving it (manual homing). `J1`…`J4`.

example.srs: SetJointPosition J4, 0

steps.name: CNC Program
steps.description: Follow a toolpath generated from a DXF or SVG file.
notes: Follows a toolpath generated from a DXF or SVG file. The toolpath itself is edited in the CNC builder and travels in the text as an `@with {…}` line.
At run time the toolpath expands into linear moves (and thread moves). Run from step cannot start inside it.

errors.label: Motion fault
errors.when: The motion system reports a fault (fatal).

errors.label: Joint limit
errors.when: The target is outside a joint's soft limits (fatal).

errors.label: Driver disconnected
errors.when: The motor driver is not connected (fatal).

example.srs: CncProgram "part.dxf", safeZ=5

steps.name: Save Position
steps.description: Store the current position in a Points list or a saved point.
steps.syntax: SavePosition $<list>[, mode=replace|append|insert|set][, index=…][, source=actual|target] | SavePosition point <name>

params.label: Saved point
params.help: Overwritten (or created) with the current position; recorded in the points history.

notes: Stores where the robot is ("Here"), expressed in the program's active local frame, so a later move under the same local lands on the same spot.
Into a Points list: `mode=replace` (the list becomes exactly this pose), `append`, `insert` or `set` (at `index=`). A list that does not exist is created.
`SavePosition point <name>` overwrites a saved point (or creates it); the change is recorded in the points history.
`source=target` stores the last commanded target instead of the measured position.

errors.label: List index out of range
errors.when: `index=` is outside the list (catchable).

errors.label: List step does not fit the list
errors.when: The variable is not a Points list (fatal).

errors.label: Point not found
errors.when: A point linked by id no longer exists.

example.srs:
var taught: list point
SavePosition $taught, mode=append
SavePosition point Pick1

steps.name: Set Speed (Linear)
steps.description: Set the linear move speed, accel and decel.
notes: Sets the default speed, acceleration and deceleration for later linear moves (Move Linear, Jump Linear legs, arcs). A move's own `speed=` overrides it for that move only.
Not run in background programs.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs: SetSpeedL 200, accel=800, decel=800

steps.name: Set Speed (Joint)
steps.description: Set the joint move speed, accel and decel.
notes: Sets the default speed, acceleration and deceleration for later joint moves.
Not run in background programs.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs: SetSpeedJ 60, accel=200

steps.name: Set Blend Radius
steps.description: Set the default corner radius for later blended moves.
notes: Sets the default corner radius used by later moves that blend without giving their own radius.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
SetBlendRadius 5
MoveL Approach, blend=on

steps.name: Set Speed Factor
steps.description: Scale this program's move speeds by a percentage.

params.label: Speed factor
params.help: Never exceeds the operator's speed override; resets to 100 when the program ends.

notes: Every later move of this program runs at *operator override × factor / 100* — single moves, blended runs, jump legs, arcs and a move resumed after a stop.
It can only slow a program down: values are clamped to 1–100 %. Manual moves and jogging are never affected.
Readable as `$program.speedFactor`; back to 100 when the run ends.
Not run in background programs.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
SetSpeedFactor 25     # slow first cycle
MoveL Pick1
SetSpeedFactor 100

steps.name: Set Tool
steps.description: Change the active tool used by later moves.

params.label: Tool
params.help: None = no tool offset.

notes: Makes a tool (TCP offset) active for later moves; points are reached with the tool's tip. None = no tool offset.
Not run in background programs.

example.srs:
SetTool Gripper
MoveL Pick1

steps.name: Set Local
steps.description: Activate a local coordinate frame for later moves.
notes: Activates a local coordinate frame: later targets and offsets are interpreted in it.
A single move can use another frame with `local=`.
Not run in background programs.

example.srs:
SetLocal Fixture1
MoveL here, offset=(x=10, y=10)
ClearLocal

steps.name: Clear Local
steps.description: Return later moves to the world frame.
notes: Returns later moves to the world (base) frame.
Not run in background programs.

example.srs: ClearLocal

steps.name: If Condition
steps.description: Run steps only when a condition holds, with else-if and else branches.
notes: Branches are tested top to bottom; the first whose condition holds runs, else the `else` branch.
A condition is an ordinary expression; non-zero is true. Its top-level `and` / `or` become the separate condition rows the Blocks editor shows.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
var count = 0
if $count >= 12
  status "Tray full"
elif $count > 8
  status warning "Almost full"
else
  $count = $count + 1
end

steps.name: Switch
steps.description: Run the case whose value equals an expression.

params.label: Value
params.help: Evaluated once; compared with each case value.

notes: The value is evaluated once; the first case with an equal value (within 1e-9) runs, otherwise `default`. There is no fall-through.
Numbers only — test text with `if $s.contains(…)`.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
var grade = 1
switch $grade
case 1
  MoveL Place1
case 2, 3
  MoveL stack Bins[0]
default
  raise "Unknown grade {$grade}"
end

steps.name: Loop
steps.description: Repeat steps a number of times, for each list element, or while a condition holds.
steps.syntax: repeat <n>|forever [as $i] … end | for $v[, $i] in $list … end | while <condition> … end

params.label: Count
params.help: 0 = forever.

params.label: Value variable
params.help: Number/Boolean lists: the element. Other lists: the index.

notes: `repeat n` runs the body n times (`as $i` counts from 0); `repeat forever` (count 0) runs until stopped or left with `break`.

`for $v, $i in $list` walks a list. Number and Boolean lists give the element in `$v`; Point and Record lists give the index, so read the element as `$list[$i]`. Write `for _, $i in $list` when you only want the index.
`while <condition>` re-checks the condition before every pass.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
var vals: list number = (1, 2, 3)
var sum = 0
repeat 3 as $i
  MoveL grid Tray[$i], offset=(z=10)
end
for $v, $i in $vals
  $sum = $sum + $v
end
while $stb.in1 == 0
  Wait 10ms
end

steps.name: Break / Next
steps.description: Leave the enclosing loop, or skip to its next iteration.
notes: `break` leaves the nearest enclosing loop; `continue` ends this pass (a count loop counts it, a for-each moves to the next element, a while re-checks its condition).
Branches and Try bodies between the step and the loop are simply left. It never crosses a routine boundary.

example.srs:
repeat forever
  if $stb.in2
    break
  end
  Wait 50ms
end

steps.name: Try
steps.description: Run steps; on a runtime error retry them or run the catch steps.

params.label: Catch only

options.label: Arc points are in a line

params.help: Empty = every catchable error. A Raise Error code may be typed in.

notes: When a step inside the body fails with a catchable code — at any depth, including called routines — the body is abandoned; while retries are left it runs again from the top after `delay=`; then the message and code go into the catch variables and the catch steps run.
An empty catch ignores the error. The program continues after the Try either way.
`only=(…)` limits which codes are caught; others go to the next enclosing Try. A failure inside the catch also goes outward.
Fatal codes (motion faults, e-stop, user stop, unknown variables, syntax errors) are never caught.

example.srs:
var msg: string
var code: string
try retry=2, delay=500ms
  Wait until $stb.in1, timeout=2s, onTimeout=error
catch $msg, code=$code
  status warning "Gave up: {$msg}"
end

steps.name: Raise Error
steps.description: Fail with a message — caught by an enclosing Try, otherwise ends the program.

params.label: Code
params.help: An identifier a Try can filter on.

notes: Fails with your message and code (default `userError`). An enclosing Try that catches the code takes over; otherwise the program ends with Error.
A code of your own is always catchable.

errors.label: Raised error
errors.when: The default code — or any identifier you give with `code=`.

example.srs:
var count = 0
if $count == 0
  raise "No parts found", code=noParts
end

steps.name: Call Routine
steps.description: Run a routine, then continue.

params.label: Arguments
params.help: One expression per in / in-out parameter (a template for a text parameter), evaluated before the call.

params.label: Outputs
params.help: Out / in-out parameters copied into your variables when the routine returns.

notes: Runs a routine program, then continues with the next step.
`in` / `inout` arguments are evaluated in the caller's scope before the routine starts; when it ends (last step or Return), mapped `out` / `inout` parameters are copied into the caller's variables.
A routine is a boundary: Go To Label and Break / Next inside it never reach the caller.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
var ok: bool = off
call PickPart(slot=3), out picked=$ok

steps.name: Return
steps.description: Leave the routine (or end the program).
notes: In a routine: leave it now (out parameters are copied back). In a main or background program: finish with Complete.

example.srs:
if not $stb.in1
  return
end

steps.name: End Program
steps.description: Finish the program now, from anywhere.
notes: Finishes the program with Complete from any depth (loops, routines, Try), with the message as the final status text. A background program ends only itself.

example.srs:
var count = 0
exit "Done after {$count} parts"

steps.name: Label
steps.description: Mark a place Go To Label can jump to.
notes: Marks a place Go To Label can jump to. The name must be unique in the program.

example.srs:
label retry
Wait until $stb.in1, timeout=5s
goto retry

steps.name: Go To Label
steps.description: Jump to a Label.
notes: Jumps to a label in the same program (or the same routine). Prefer loops where they fit — they read better and keep the structure visible.

example.srs:
label again
MoveL Pick1
goto again

steps.name: Pause Program
steps.description: Pause — the operator continues or stops from the monitor.
notes: Pauses the program (status Stopped) with its place kept; the operator continues or stops it from the monitor.

example.srs:
status "Check the gripper, then press Continue"
pause

steps.name: Note
steps.description: A note or section header — not executed.
notes: Not executed and not counted as a step. `## text` is a section header the editor can collapse; a comment paragraph followed by a blank line is a note.

example.srs:
## Pick
# Approach from above, then grip.

MoveL Pick1

steps.name: Set Variable
steps.description: Assign a value or expression to a variable.

params.label: Value
params.help: An expression; a template for a text variable.

notes: Evaluates the expression and stores it. A text variable takes a template in quotes: `$label = "Bin {$i}"`.
Comparisons yield 1 / 0, so they can be stored in a boolean directly.
Properties (`$robot.x`…), IO names and computed variables cannot be assigned.

errors.label: Write to a computed variable
errors.when: The target is a computed variable (fatal).

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
var count = 0
var label: string
$count = $count + 1
$label = "Bin {$count}"

steps.name: List
steps.description: Append, insert, remove, set, sort or copy list elements.

params.label: Action
params.value: append | insert | removeAt | clear | set | setField | sort | reverse | copyFrom

params.label: Value
params.help: For Number and Boolean lists.

params.label: Fields
params.help: For Point and Record lists. Append with no fields on a Points list appends the current position.

params.label: Sort by field
params.help: Empty = the element value.

notes: Number / Boolean lists take a value; Point / Record lists take fields (`x=…, y=…`). `$pts.append()` with no fields appends the current position.
Everything is evaluated before the list changes, so a failing step leaves the list as it was. The declared list is never changed — a re-run starts from it.

errors.label: List index out of range
errors.when: The index is outside the list (catchable).

errors.label: List step does not fit the list
errors.when: The step does not fit the list: fields on a Number list, a value for a Points list, an incompatible copy (fatal).

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
var vals: list number
var pts: list point
$vals.append(5)
$vals.sort(by=value, desc)
$pts.append(x=$robot.x, y=$robot.y, z=50)
$pts[0].z = 30

steps.name: Stopwatch
steps.description: Start, stop or reset a stopwatch variable.
notes: A stopwatch variable holds elapsed milliseconds while it runs; `stop` freezes it, `reset` sets it to 0.

example.srs:
var lap: stopwatch
stopwatch start $lap
MoveL Pick1
stopwatch stop $lap
status "Move took {$lap} ms"

steps.name: Wait
steps.description: Wait for a time, or until a condition holds.
steps.syntax: Wait <ms> | Wait until <condition>[, timeout=…][, timedOut=$v][, onTimeout=continue|error]

params.label: Timeout
params.help: Empty or 0 = wait forever.

notes: `Wait 500ms` pauses for a time. `Wait until <condition>` holds until the condition is true, checked every tick.
With `timeout=`, `timedOut=$v` is set to 1 when time ran out. `onTimeout=continue` (default) carries on; `onTimeout=error` fails with `waitTimeout`, which a Try can catch.
A condition that holds on the tick the timeout falls due counts as met.

errors.label: Wait timed out
errors.when: Condition wait timed out with `onTimeout=error` (catchable).

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
var late: bool = off
Wait 250ms
Wait until $stb.in1 == 1, timeout=5s, timedOut=$late

steps.name: Set Output
steps.description: Turn a digital output on or off, toggle it or pulse it.

params.label: On
params.help: An expression: non-zero = on.

params.label: Pulse
params.help: Set for this long, then flip back. Empty = hold.

notes: Cards: `stb` (driver board outputs), `relay` (USB relay channels), `io` (an IO device such as an Arduino Nano — name the device).
The value may be `on`, `off`, `toggle` or an expression in parentheses (non-zero = on).
`pulse=` sets the output for that long, then flips it back. `blocking=on` waits for the pulse to finish; otherwise the program moves on and the flip-back happens in the background.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
SetOutput stb 1 on
SetOutput relay 2 on, pulse=250ms, blocking=on
SetOutput io Arduino_Nano 7 toggle

steps.name: Tare Load Cell
steps.description: Zero a load cell.
notes: Zeroes a load cell: its current raw reading becomes the tare offset.

example.srs: Tare device=Arduino_Nano, pin=2

steps.name: Read Load Cell
steps.description: Read a load cell into a variable.
notes: Reads the calibrated weight into a variable in the chosen unit (grams by default). In expressions a load cell can also be read live as `$io.<device>.<pin name>` (grams).

example.srs:
var grams = 0
ReadLoadCell $grams, device=Arduino_Nano, pin=2, unit=g

steps.name: Start Recording
steps.description: Record a load cell into a list variable.
notes: Starts capturing a load cell. The samples arrive in the list when Stop Recording runs, as records `{t, v, r}`. The recording also shows in the app's Recordings browser.

example.srs:
var rec: list record
StartRecording $rec, device=Arduino_Nano, pin=2
MoveL Pick1, offset=(z=-5)
StopRecording device=Arduino_Nano, pin=2

steps.name: Stop Recording
steps.description: Stop a recording and store its samples.
notes: Stops the recording this program started on that load cell and fills its list variable.

example.srs: StopRecording device=Arduino_Nano, pin=2

steps.name: Export Data
steps.description: Write variables to a CSV or JSON file.
notes: Writes one row per column (`"name" = value`) to a CSV or JSON file on the controller. A value can be an expression, `list $var` or `image $var`.
The path is a template (`{$time_ms}` etc.); a relative path is relative to the controller's folder. Missing folders are created.

example.srs:
var grams = 0
var rec: list record
ExportData csv "logs/run-{$time_ms}.csv"
  "weight" = $grams
  "series" = list $rec
end

steps.name: Aux Move
steps.description: Move an aux axis by a distance or a number of steps.
steps.syntax: AuxMove device=…, axis=…, distance=…|steps=…[, unit=mm|deg][, velocity=…][, absolute=on][, wait=off][, until=…]

params.label: Device
params.help: The aux IO card.

params.label: Unit
params.help: Empty = raw steps.

params.label: Distance
params.help: In the unit above.

params.label: Steps
params.help: Used when no unit is set; the sign is the direction.

params.label: Stop condition
params.help: Watched every tick while the move runs, e.g. $io.Nano.Load >= 2000.

params.label: Position variable
params.help: Receives the axis position (mm / deg, or steps).

params.label: Fired flag
params.help: Set to 1 if the condition fired during the move, else 0.

notes: Moves an auxiliary stepper axis by `distance=` in `unit=` (mm or deg) or by raw `steps=`; the sign is the direction. `absolute=on` moves to a position instead.
`wait=on` (default) holds the program until the motor finishes; `wait=off` fires and forgets.
Takes a stop condition only when it waits.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
AuxMove device=Aux_Stepper, axis=0, unit=mm, distance=25, velocity=20
AuxMove device=Aux_Stepper, axis=0, steps=-400, until=$stb.in2

steps.name: Aux Continuous Run
steps.description: Run an aux axis continuously until an Aux Stop.

params.label: Device
params.help: The aux IO card.

params.label: Velocity
params.help: The sign is the direction.

notes: Runs an aux axis at a constant velocity (sign = direction) until an Aux Stop.

example.srs:
AuxContinuous device=Aux_Stepper, axis=2, velocity=-10
Wait until $stb.in3
AuxStop device=Aux_Stepper, axis=2

steps.name: Aux Stop
steps.description: Stop aux axis motion — ramped or immediate.

params.label: Device
params.help: The aux IO card.

notes: Stops an aux axis with a ramp (`decel=`), or at once with `immediate=on`.

example.srs: AuxStop device=Aux_Stepper, axis=2, immediate=on

steps.name: Aux Motor Enable
steps.description: Enable or disable the motor drivers of an aux card.

params.label: Device
params.help: The aux IO card.

notes: Enables or disables the motor drivers of an aux card. A disabled motor can be turned by hand.

example.srs: AuxEnable on, device=Aux_Stepper, axis=0

steps.name: Gripper
steps.description: Open, close or grip to a jaw gap.
steps.syntax: GripperAction open|close|to <mm>[, device=…, axis=…][, velocity=…][, until=…]

params.label: Device
params.help: The aux IO card.

params.label: Stop condition
params.help: Watched every tick while the move runs, e.g. $io.Nano.Load >= 2000.

params.label: Position variable
params.help: Receives the axis position (mm / deg, or steps).

params.label: Fired flag
params.help: Set to 1 if the condition fired during the move, else 0.

notes: Drives a gripper-role aux axis to its configured open or closed gap, or to a jaw gap in mm (`to 25`).
With a stop condition the jaws stop when it holds — for example close until a load cell reads a grip force.

errors.label: Unknown variable
errors.when: An expression names a variable that does not exist (fatal).

errors.label: Expression error
errors.when: An expression does not parse (fatal).

example.srs:
GripperAction open
GripperAction close, until=$io.Arduino_Nano.Input_1 >= 300
GripperAction to 25

steps.name: Conveyor
steps.description: Run a conveyor forward or reverse, or stop it.

params.label: Device
params.help: The aux IO card.

notes: Runs a conveyor-role aux axis forward or in reverse, or stops it.

example.srs:
ConveyorAction forward, device=Aux_Stepper, axis=2
Wait until $stb.in1
ConveyorAction stop, device=Aux_Stepper, axis=2

steps.name: Rotary Index
steps.description: Index a rotary axis a number of positions.

params.label: Device
params.help: The aux IO card.

notes: Turns a rotary-role aux axis by `count` positions in the given direction (+1 or −1).

example.srs: RotaryIndex +1, count=3, device=Aux_Stepper, axis=3

steps.name: Run Vision
steps.description: Run a vision program and write its results into variables.

params.label: Tool outputs
params.help: Rows of tool · value → variable.

notes: Runs a vision program on a fresh camera frame and writes tool results into variables, one row per `tool.value -> $var`. Values include any key of the tool's values (`angle`, `count`, `x`…), `passed`, `found`, `status`, and the lists `points`, `items`, `cells`, `lines`, `pose`.
`frame=` sets the coordinates of positions written: `pixel` (default), `normalized` (0–1) or `robot` (mm on the camera's calibration plane — needs a calibrated camera).
`pass=$v` gets 1 when every tool that counts toward the pass passed. Variables named in rows are created if not declared.

errors.label: Vision timed out
errors.when: No fresh result in time (default 30 s) (catchable).

errors.label: Vision failed
errors.when: The vision processor is lost, or the robot frame is not available (catchable).

example.srs:
var ok: bool = off
var edgeAngle = 0
var cells: list record
RunVision Detect_Parts, frame=robot, pass=$ok
  Top_edge.angle -> $edgeAngle
  Slots.cells -> $cells
end

steps.name: Capture Image
steps.description: Store the current camera frame in an image variable.
notes: Stores the current camera frame (JPEG) in an image variable — to send over HTTP, hand to a plugin, export or show on a display page.

errors.label: Vision failed
errors.when: The camera has no frame (catchable).

example.srs:
var photo: image
CaptureImage $photo, camera=Top_Camera

steps.name: Save Image
steps.description: Save a camera snapshot to a file.
notes: Saves a camera snapshot to a file on the controller. The path is a template: `"shots/{$time_ms}.jpg"`.

errors.label: Vision failed
errors.when: The camera has no frame (catchable).

example.srs: SaveImage "shots/part-{$time_ms}.jpg", camera=Top_Camera

steps.name: Start Background
steps.description: Start a background program in parallel.
notes: Starts a background program running in parallel with this one. Background programs skip motion, tool and homing steps.

example.srs: StartBackground Conveyor_Watch

steps.name: Stop Background
steps.description: Stop a background program.
notes: Stops a running background program.

example.srs: StopBackground Conveyor_Watch

steps.name: Wait for Background
steps.description: Wait until a background program finishes.
notes: Holds this program until the background program finishes.

example.srs:
StartBackground Conveyor_Watch
WaitForBackground Conveyor_Watch

steps.name: HTTP Request
steps.description: POST JSON to a server and read values from the reply.
steps.syntax: HttpRequest "<url>"[, wait=on][, timeout=…] send … receive … end
notes: POSTs a JSON object built from the `send` rows (`"key" = expression`, `list $var`, `image $var`) and, with `wait=on`, reads `receive "key" -> $var` values from the JSON reply.
An empty or non-JSON reply is not a failure. With `wait=off` the request never fails.

errors.label: HTTP request failed
errors.when: Network error or a non-2xx status (catchable).

errors.label: HTTP request timed out
errors.when: No reply in time (catchable).

example.srs:
var count = 0
var reply = 0
HttpRequest "http://192.168.4.10:8080/report", wait=on, timeout=5s
  send "count" = $count
  receive "next" -> $reply
end

steps.name: HTTP Receive
steps.description: Wait for an HTTP POST to a named webhook.

params.label: Name
params.help: Other machines POST to /webhook/<name>.

notes: Waits for another machine to POST JSON to `/webhook/<name>` on the controller, then copies `receive` keys into variables.

errors.label: HTTP receive timed out
errors.when: Nothing arrived in time (catchable).

example.srs:
var x = 0
HttpReceive "orders", timeout=60s
  receive "x" -> $x
end

steps.name: Status Update
steps.description: Publish a message, warning or error to the monitor.
notes: Publishes a message to the monitor and the run log: `status "…"`, `status warning "…"`, `status error "…"`. The text is a template. An error status does not stop the program.

example.srs:
var count = 0
status "Placed {$count} parts"
status warning "Tray almost full"

steps.name: Prompt
steps.description: Ask the operator: show a message with buttons and an optional input.
steps.syntax: prompt "<message>"[, title=…][, buttons=(…)][, input=number|text][, result=$v][, value=$v][, timeout=…]

params.label: Button variable
params.help: A number variable gets the button index (from 0); a text variable gets its label.

params.label: Timeout
params.help: 0 = wait forever.

params.label: On timeout press
params.help: Button index chosen on timeout. Empty = fail (catchable).

notes: Shows the operator a dialog with 1–4 buttons and optionally a number or text input, and waits. A number result variable gets the button index (from 0), a text one its label.
With `timeout=` and `onTimeout=<button>` the button is pressed on timeout; without a button the prompt fails `promptTimeout`.
The dialog appears in the app on any screen. A Stop keeps it on screen but refuses answers; Continue shows it again.

errors.label: Prompt timed out
errors.when: Timed out with no timeout button (catchable).

example.srs:
var choice = 0
var qty = 0
prompt "Load the tray, then continue", title="Setup", buttons=("Continue", "Skip"), result=$choice
prompt "How many parts?", input=number, default=10, min=1, max=50, value=$qty

steps.name: Plugin
steps.description: A step provided by an installed plugin.

params.label: Parameters
params.help: Typed by the plugin manifest.

params.label: Timeout
params.help: Empty = the manifest default; 0 = none.

notes: Runs a step an installed plugin declares in its manifest. Parameter rows: unquoted = an expression, quoted = exact text. Output rows `key -> $var` write the plugin's results.
The program waits (without blocking anything else) until the plugin answers. Background programs can run plugin steps.

errors.label: Plugin not running
errors.when: The plugin is not running (catchable).

errors.label: Plugin step failed
errors.when: The plugin answered with an error (catchable).

errors.label: Plugin step timed out
errors.when: No answer in time (catchable).

example.srs:
var w = 0
plugin scale.weigh, timeout=5s
  samples = 5
  unit = "g"
  grams -> $w
end

errorCodes.label: Wait timed out
errorCodes.description: A condition Wait with `onTimeout=error` reached its timeout.

errorCodes.label: Vision timed out
errorCodes.description: Run Vision got no fresh result in time.

errorCodes.label: Vision failed
errorCodes.description: The vision processor was lost, the robot output frame is not available, or a camera had no frame (Capture / Save Image).

errorCodes.label: HTTP request failed
errorCodes.description: HTTP Request: network error or a non-2xx status.

errorCodes.label: HTTP request timed out
errorCodes.description: HTTP Request: no reply in time.

errorCodes.label: HTTP receive timed out
errorCodes.description: HTTP Receive: nothing was posted in time.

errorCodes.label: Plugin step failed
errorCodes.description: A plugin step or function answered with an error.

errorCodes.label: Plugin step timed out
errorCodes.description: A plugin step did not answer in time.

errorCodes.label: Plugin not running
errorCodes.description: The plugin is installed but not running.

errorCodes.label: Prompt timed out
errorCodes.description: A Prompt timed out and has no timeout button.

errorCodes.label: Point not found
errorCodes.description: A template or list target names no saved point, a Points list is empty, or a via point is unknown.

errorCodes.label: Arc points are in a line
errorCodes.description: Move Arc: start, via and end are on one line, or two are the same.

errorCodes.label: List index out of range
errorCodes.description: List / Save Position: the index is outside the list.

errorCodes.label: Raised error
errorCodes.description: The default code of Raise Error. Any identifier you raise yourself is also catchable.

errorCodes.label: Motion fault
errorCodes.description: The motion system reported a fault.

errorCodes.label: Joint limit
errorCodes.description: A target is outside a joint's soft limits.

errorCodes.label: Driver disconnected
errorCodes.description: The motor driver disconnected.

errorCodes.label: Emergency stop
errorCodes.description: The emergency stop was pressed.

errorCodes.label: Stopped by user
errorCodes.description: The operator stopped the program.

errorCodes.label: Unknown variable
errorCodes.description: An expression names a variable, property or IO point that does not exist.

errorCodes.label: Expression error
errorCodes.description: An expression does not parse (also `unknownFunction` / `badArity`).

errorCodes.label: Write to a computed variable
errorCodes.description: A step tried to write a computed variable.

errorCodes.label: List step does not fit the list
errorCodes.description: A List or Save Position step does not fit its list (an authoring error).

parse.meaning: Not valid here (with what was expected).
A statement word that does not exist (with "did you mean …").
A named value the step does not have.
The wrong kind of value: text where a number belongs, an option that does not exist, an expression without parentheses in a positional slot.
From the expression checker, pointing inside the expression (also `unknownFunction`, `badArity`).
An `end` with no block to close.
A text variable assigned an expression, or a number variable assigned text.
An underscore-form name fits more than one item — write the quoted name.

parse.code: unknownPoint / unknownTool / unknownRoutine / unknownGrid / unknownDevice / unknownLabel …
parse.meaning: Warning: the name does not resolve (yet); it is kept.
Warning: an `@with` key that is not a field (dropped).

validation.code: unknownPoint, unknownTool, unknownLocal, unknownRoutine, unknownVisionProgram, unknownGrid, unknownStack, unknownProgram
validation.meaning: A referenced item does not exist.
Go To Label names no label / two labels share a name.
An expression names something that does not exist.
An expression does not parse.
A property or IO name used as a write target or declared as a variable.
A required field is empty.
A loop or branch with no steps.
A routine calls itself (directly or indirectly).
Break / Next outside a loop (or crossing a routine boundary).
Computed-variable rules (see Data and variables).
A routine argument or output that does not fit the routine's parameters.
A field the step does not support (e.g. a stop condition on Move Arc).
Run Vision robot frame without a calibrated camera / an unknown frame.

validation.code: unknownPlugin / unknownPluginStep / pluginParamMissing / pluginParamEnum / pluginOutputType / unknownPluginFunction
validation.meaning: Plugin step and function checks.
A routine parameter with no argument keeps its declared value.
Two Switch cases share a value.
The plugin is installed but not running.
A grid or stack whose steps are all zero.
A background program overwrites a saved point.
Housekeeping hints.

functions.name: max

functions.name: clamp

functions.name: round

functions.name: floor

functions.name: ceil
functions.description: Round up

functions.name: trunc

functions.name: mod

functions.name: cos

functions.name: len

functions.name: avg

properties.name: $robot.faulted

properties.name: $robot.driverConnected

properties.name: $robot.joint1Referenced
properties.description: 1 once J1/X is homed or set to a known value

properties.name: $robot.joint2Referenced
properties.description: 1 once Horizontal/Y is homed or set to a known value

properties.name: $robot.joint3Referenced
properties.description: 1 once Vertical/Z is homed or set to a known value

properties.name: $robot.joint4Referenced
properties.description: 1 once J4/RZ is homed or set to a known value

properties.name: $program.runCount

properties.name: $program.stepIndex
properties.description: Completed top-level steps in this run

properties.name: $program.speedFactor
